naascott

There are few things I want to see when I'm looking for good DP:

- it can be located on swap zone

- FO zone can be created below it ( short scenario)

- also I like to see CP above strong DP - if price is compressed above,
then it is more likely that price will be reversed on this DP - it is
only fresh DP in the area

DP is a barrier to ITs, because another sellers are waiting on this
level (short scenario), so they need to do their manipulations before
price reaches it - they need to create LQ and when they do that we see
reversal patterns, FO zones etc.

bobyv87

FL and PAZ between them work in every TF, therefore some FLs are more
important than others, smaller or bigger FLs. There are diffrent
cycles.

It's quite difficult to learn spot all of this correctly but with a lot
of practice it will become clear. And don't forget to look left:

Markers are usually small FLs - ITs use them to reverse price before DP.
 I like to see when price bouces from this level few times - it creates
FO zone below DP which provides LQ for ITs. I enter on FO to DP after
confirmation - in this case it was eng into CPPAZ on approach. I thik
that after this reversal PA SL can be above DP (grey box - because it is
 FL in itself - you can see this on m1 chart). But if situation is not
very clear then you may use wider SL.

bobyv87

To define cycles you have to evaluate importance of FL. I'm not an
expert at this yet, because I still have some things to learn about PAZ,
 but with practice I am more and more often able to spot this correctly
on chart. I find it difficult to explain though. You have to think
about space between FL's. When you find space that is limited from both
 sides by FL's, then after eng you expect price to go to next FL in
direction of eng. Befere this happens price creates Fls as it retraces,
but these FLs don't affect main move. They work in different cycles.

Blue box that you marked is not FTR. It is reaction to DP on QM lvl. It
is high that didn't engulf anything. Price engulfed FL at 3 and FL was
made at 4.

smimon

I learned all of this from free RTM, and by doing price reading on historic data. I still have a lot to learn though .

bobyv I started to notice FO zones when I tried to think about
 ITs and how they need to create LQ by hunting for stops and making BO
traders open wrong positions. I don't trade when I see only FO zone - it
 is not enough. FO zone is most of the times just a part of good setup.

I can distinguish 2 types of setups with FO zones:

- First one is setup where there is already a FO zone created before
price arrives at particular lvl. For example there is nice fresh FTR and
 sing high / swing higs below it ( short scenario ). You definitely need
 confirmation PA in setup like this one on approach and reaction.

- Second one is creating LQ after price shown reversal signals (ENG).

author: Michal238
text:
This folder contains everything related to trading, but majority of charts is FL analysis.

Number of folders is so big, because I have many setups saved in
separate folders, and I make new folder for every session on FT2

I realized recently that I'm pretty bad at decision making, I'm not
patient enough on live charts, and I tend to make the same mistakes many
 times due to loose analysis.

So I set some rules regarding my analysis during practise on FT2:

I test one pair at a time and I have 3 separate charts. One is for
general HTF view and I mark most important lvls and FLs on it.

Second chart is for LTF FL analysis - sometimes it gets messy and that is why I need more than one chart.

On third chart I mark S/R flips, swaps lvls - it is easy to miss them when chart is not neat and clean.

Doing this I'm sure that I used propely my best analysis tools, and I wont do mistakes that could easily been avoided.

And this is how I'm going to improve my decision making:

- I take screenshots with my analysis and mark best places to look for PA

- as price is approaching my lvl, I make decision - do I wait for
confirmation or can I TT? why? I write this on screenshot. Decision is
made.

- let's say that I took TT. At this point I have marked on chart
different sized FL that were formed on approach - I decide where is my
TP1 and where

are potential trouble areas

- I make screen after TP1 , and then after every continuation ENG, or reversal ENG.

- reversal ENG - I close my trade

- continuation ENG - I make decision - where I'll let price retrace to, before closing my trade? where in next FL?

As price is moving away (or towards) my entry I mark new FLs that are
created, I mark CP, and strong SD lvls / ignored SD lvls, using always

the same colors. I don't want to miss/ forget anything. Also I do this to develop habists:

strong SD lvls formed against me ----> look for exit

CP between my entry, and current price ----> I move my SL above last fresh SD lvl

FL not engulfed --> exit

etc.

I know that this is basic stuff, but sometimes I ignored important
information, because I wanted my FL analysis to be correct every single
time.

Its stupid, I know, but I have done this in the past on live account

Every trade is narrated, and I also try to think like IT - what they want to accomplish, where is LQ for them

- what are doing trend followers?

- what are doing BO traders?

- what are doing savy SD traders?

In the next month I will continue practising in this way, and what is
most important - I also want to apply this method to live charts.

In this way I will have everything propely analysed, and decisions will be made only once - I wont stay undecided at any time.

Analysis is made ---> its time to make decisions and write it down.

New piece of PA created --> make analysis marking FLs, SD, CPs ---> make decision, just like on FT2

I described briefly how my perfect price reading session looks like.
Probably I will post here example of this on real charts soon.

It is easy to just fast-forward charts not thinking much about it. Its
tempting as well - because there is a part of me that enjoys gambling.

What I want to achieve in my every single price reading session is
called "deliberate practice" - it takes big ammount of effort,

but I believe that in this way I can get great results.
